title: Khara's fight with Rama
introduction: Khara provokes Rama to fight, but Rama gives enough advise to Khara to yield up. Khara presumes that Rama is overtired to fight him back and thus enters into verbal fight. Ultimately Khara hurls a mammoth mace at Rama, which burns down all the neighbouring plants and bushes, and Rama splinters it down while it is still sky rocketing.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे एकोन त्रिंश सर्गः
Thus, this is the 29th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
खरम् तु विरथम् रामो गदा पाणिम् अवस्थितम् |
मृदु पूर्वम् महातेजाः परुषम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
kharam tu viratham rāmo gadā pāṇim avasthitam |
mṛdu pūrvam mahātejāḥ paruṣam vākyam abravīt
verses.translation: Rama, the great-resplendent, spoke these words forbiddingly albeit softly to Khara who lost his chariot but staying his course wielding a mace.
notes: Rama is said to have tested whether Khara is ready to surrender or not, at least at this stage of loosing all paraphernalia of war. Hence he is said to have talked softly but harshly to that demon.

verses.devanagari:
गज अश्व रथ संबाधे बले महति तिष्ठता |
कृतम् सुदारुणम् कर्म सर्व लोक जुगुप्सितम्
verses.iast:
gaja aśva ratha sambādhe bale mahati tiṣṭhatā |
kṛtam sudāruṇam karma sarva loka jugup.hsitam
verses.translation: "Although you hold sway over a gigantic force abounding with elephants horses and chariots, you have perpetrated heinous deeds in Dandaka forests that are loathsome to all the worlds, that is unseemliest to this soldiery.

glosses.meaning: by all, worlds, detestable - loathsome, deed

verses.devanagari:
उद्वेजनीयो भूतानाम् नृशंसः पाप कर्मकृत् |
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानाम् ईश्वरो अपि न तिष्ठति
verses.iast:
udvejanīyo bhūtānām nṛśaṃsaḥ pāpa karmakṛt |
trayāṇām api lokānām īśvaro api na tiṣṭhati
verses.translation: "One who causes suffering to living beings, besides being a transgressor and completely ruthless, he does not stand up for himself even if he were to be the lord of all the three worlds.

verses.devanagari:
कर्म लोक विरुद्धम् तु कुर्वाणम् क्षणदा चर |
तीक्ष्णम् सर्व जनो हन्ति सर्पम् दुष्टम् इव आगतम्
verses.iast:
karma loka viruddham tu kurvāṇam kṣaṇadā cara |
tīkṣṇam sarva jano hanti sarpam duṣṭam iva āgatam
verses.translation: "All people will eliminate him, oh, nightwalker, who is imperious and an infringer of worldly routine, as they would eradicate a vicious serpent, in the event of its running across them.

glosses.meaning: to world, infringing, deeds, who will be doing - an infringer of worldly routine
that came, vicious, serpent, as with

verses.devanagari:
लोभात् पापानि कुर्वाणः कामात् वा यो न बुध्यते |
हृष्टः पश्यति तस्य अन्तम् ब्राह्मणी करकात् इव
verses.iast:
lobhāt pāpāni kurvāṇaḥ kāmāt vā yo na budhyate |
hṛṣṭaḥ paśyati tasya antam brāhmaṇī karakāt iva
verses.translation: "He who goes on performing evils selfishly, obsessively, heedlessly, more so delightedly, he will see the results of his own doings, like red-tailed-lizard on its eating self-destructive hailstones, obsessively and delightedly.
notes: Hailstones are life-taking poisonous pellets to this particular red- tailed lizard, called brahmaṇi . It is still called as 'bamaani' in Bhojpuri vernacular of Hindi.

Parting with some parts of one's own accrual is lobha, and craving for that which is absolutely unavailable is moha. People tend to commit sin while protecting their own accruals as well as trying to acquire unavailable things. But any person, if goes on undertaking these evils, even after realizing that both are mistakes, it is an unpardonable crime. The metaphor of a red-tail-lizard is said to be unavailable in older scripts. There is another variation to this foot wherein the simile is with a Brahman bereft of his self-respect, and that foot reads as: bhrṣṭaḥ paśyati duḥkham sa brāhmaṇa paravān iva .
Next, implying the prospective question of Khara, viz., 'What sin I have committed?' Rama answers it in the next verse.

glosses.meaning: who, evils, while going on doing
will not, know - does not realise - heedless
what has been done - evil deed

verses.devanagari:
वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तापसान् धर्म चारिणः |
किम् नु हत्वा महाभागान् फलम् प्राप्स्यसि राक्षस
verses.iast:
vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tāpasān dharma cāriṇaḥ |
kim nu hatvā mahābhāgān phalam prāpsyasi rākṣasa
verses.translation: "The residents of Dandaka forest are the highly-propitious sages that tread the path of virtue, and oh, demon, what benefit you gain in killing them, really?
notes: Again Khara may ask, 'There are many more sinners, what will become of them, why holding me alone responsible?' For this Rama is saying that the sinners in general will get their punishment after their mortality when karmic cycle is over. But those that are not only sinners but cruel, and even abhorred by world, will ruin here only, because their merit accumulated in earlier births has come to a standstill on this earth itself. Those sinners will become like petrified trees trunks, they neither fall nor their boughs flower.

glosses.meaning: in Dandaka, forest, while living in
why [what], really, fruit [benefit,] you will gain.

verses.devanagari:
न चिरम् पाप कर्माणः क्रूरा लोक जुगुप्सिताः |
ऐश्वर्यम् प्राप्य तिष्ठन्ति शीर्ण मूला इव द्रुमाः
verses.iast:
na ciram pāpa karmāṇaḥ krūrā loka jugupsitāḥ |
aiśvaryam prāpya tiṣṭhanti śīrṇa mūlā iva drumāḥ
verses.translation: "Even if a fortune is made for a lavish living with an iota of merit, the evildoers, that too reprobates, further more those that are abominated by world will not last long, no more that petrified tree trunks.

glosses.meaning: a fortune, on getting - on making [for lavish living]
petrified, base [trunk,] of tree, as with
long-lastingly, will not, sit tight - will not last long.

verses.devanagari:
अवश्यम् लभते कर्ता फलम् पापस्य कर्मणः |
घोरम् पर्यागते काले द्रुमः पुष्पम् इव आर्तवम्
verses.iast:
avaśyam labhate kartā phalam pāpasya karmaṇaḥ |
ghoram paryāgate kāle drumaḥ puṣpam iva ārtavam
verses.translation: "One who undertakes evildoings will definitely and seasonably reap their fruits, which in his case will be ghoulish, as with the flowering of trees according to season.
notes: dhvani/allusion: That fruit of sin will not be immediate alike the a crop that yields long after sowing. Moreover the fruit of sin will be venomous, for the greedy harvester of that sin alone will devour it.

verses.devanagari:
न चिरात् प्राप्यते लोके पापानाम् कर्मणाम् फलम् |
स विषाणाम् इव अन्नानाम् भुक्तानाम् क्षणदाचर
verses.iast:
na cirāt prāpyate loke pāpānām karmaṇām phalam |
sa viṣāṇām iva annānām bhuktānām kṣaṇadācara
verses.translation: "In the world one acquires the fruit of profane acts not before long, oh, nightwalker, and it will be like venomous food devoured.
notes: dhvani/allusion: 'As one quickly acquires the results of the venomous food devoured, oh, nightwalker, the perpetrator of profane acts will acquire their fruits that quickly, in the world.' Eating food, or committing a sin is simply subjective. If one commits sin unknowingly, that will be as good as the intake of venomous food, unsuspectingly. Both the poisonous food, and committing sins will act internally and rapidly than any other ruinous inflictor. Then the sinner, or the consumer of poisonous food will acquire an inconsolable wretched state.

glosses.meaning: devoured, with, venom, food, as with

verses.devanagari:
पापम् आचरताम् घोरम् लोकस्य अप्रियम् इच्छ्हताम् |
अहम् आसादितो राज्ञा प्राणान् हन्तुम् निशाचर
verses.iast:
pāpam ācaratām ghoram lokasya apriyam icchhatām |
aham āsādito rājñā prāṇān hantum niśācara
verses.translation: "I am the king who arrived to exterminate the lives of those that perpetrate hideous sins, and even of those that wish to do evils to the disapprobation of world.
notes: The word 'raaj~na' is 'sent by some king' for it is in fifth case. Whereas the word 'raajaa' is 'as a king I have come...' This is as appearing in some mms. Dharmaakuutam uses 'raaj~naa' and says: : anena loka upadrava karaḥ rājñā avaśyam śikṣaṇīyam iti sūcitam | and he goes on quoting vidura nīti Vidura's morals in Maha Bharata: gururātmavatām śāstā śāstā durātmanām | antaḥ praccanna pāpānām śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ ||

glosses.meaning: world's, not, approbatory, those wishful of

verses.devanagari:
अद्य भित्वा मया मुक्ताः शराः कांचन भूषणाः |
विदार्य अतिपतिष्यन्ति वल्मीकम् इव पन्नगाः
verses.iast:
adya bhitvā mayā muktāḥ śarāḥ kāṃcana bhūṣaṇāḥ |
vidārya atipatiṣyanti valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
verses.translation: "Now, my arrows that are decorated in gold will be released on you like snakes rebounding from a snake-pit, and they will tear you asunder, and on riving you they will bounce back into my quivers.
notes: dhvani/allusion: My arrows can pierce through your body, not only your body but to the core of earth, and they bounce back to re-enter my quivers like the snakes that emerge from snake pits and return to their pits when their task is over. Or, when these arrows enter your body that is akin to a snake pit, they will kill all the sins lying like snakes inside that body of yours, and return to my quivers.

glosses.meaning: by me, released, in gold, decorated
out, they fall - they go out, bounce back.

verses.devanagari:
ये त्वया दण्डकारण्ये भक्षिता धर्म चारिणः |
तान् अद्य निहतः संख्ये स सैन्यो अनुगमिष्यसि
verses.iast:
ye tvayā daṇḍakāraṇye bhakṣitā dharma cāriṇaḥ |
tān adya nihataḥ saṃkhye sa sainyo anugamiṣyasi
verses.translation: "Now eliminated in war, you along with your army will tread behind those sages that were treading the path of virtue, on whom you have so far feasted in Dandaka forest.
notes: dhvani/allusion: A kind of assurance is sounded here by Rama's words in saying that Khara will be absolved of his sins. Those that are eliminated by Rama are sure to get salvation. Here not only Khara but also entire army is going to get that salvation, if Khara surrenders at least at this stage. In Skanda Purana it is said: rāma vidḍhā niśācarā bāṇaiḥ su tāḍitāḥ | rāmam āsādya samare sāyujya padavīm gatāḥ || skānda purāṇa But this sāyujua, salvation or getting to heavens is of a variety. In war those that sacrifice themselves in the fire of arrows will get indra loka. Those that conduct warfare unhappily thinking that death is the only result of war they get gandharva loka. Those that retreat or go begging for their lives and yet killed, they get guhya loka, and those that are fully aware of Kshatriya dharma and conduct righteous warfare they go to brahma loka. So says Maha Bharata. The same is said Bhagavad Gita yam yam vā api smaran bhāvam tyajatyante kalebaram | tam tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad bhāva bhāvitaḥ || Gita 8-6.

glosses.meaning: in tow, you will follow - tread behind.

verses.devanagari:
अद्य त्वाम् निहतम् बाणैः पश्यन्तु परमर्षयः |
निरयस्थम् विमानस्था ये त्वया निहता पुरा
verses.iast:
adya tvām nihatam bāṇaiḥ paśyantu paramarṣayaḥ |
nirayastham vimānasthā ye tvayā nihatā purā
verses.translation: "Let the supreme sages who were earlier slain by you may now see abiding on their aircrafts, your abidance in hellish death pangs when assaulted with my arrows.
notes: The word nirayastham is literally 'in hell of Yama' but here it is the hell-like situation caused by Rama's arrows. If the literal meaning of 'in hell' is taken the above assurance of salvation etc., will be futile, hence, it is 'hellish pangs' by the hit of arrows.

glosses.meaning: earlier, by you, who are, slain

verses.devanagari:
प्रहरस्व यथा कामम् कुरु यत्नम् कुलाधम |
अद्य ते पातयिष्यामि शिरः ताल फलम् यथा
verses.iast:
praharasva yathā kāmam kuru yatnam kulādhama |
adya te pātayiṣyāmi śiraḥ tāla phalam yathā
verses.translation: "Attack me as you wish... make an effort... you the knave of your clan... now I am going to toss your head down like a palm-fruit..." Thus Rama addressed Khara.
notes: It is questioned whether Rama is self-eulogizing when talking this way to Khara. It is contradicted saying that yuddha kāle vīra vādasya sva parākrama anusāreṇa utsāha abhivṛdhyartham para tiraskāra artham ca - ātma stuti - karaṇe doṣa abhāvāt | dk 'there is nothing wrong in foretelling how brave a warrior is and it will not come under self-praise, in war...' and the commentator goes on quoting many references, for e.g., Karna in Maha Bharata says: śūrāḥ garjanbti satatam prāvṛṣi iva balāhakāḥ | 'brave ones will be regularly thundering like thundering clouds...'

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण क्रुद्धः संरक्त लोचनः |
प्रति उवाच ततो रामम् प्रहसन् क्रोध मूर्चितः
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu rāmeṇa kruddhaḥ saṃrakta locanaḥ |
prati uvāca tato rāmam prahasan krodha mūrcitaḥ
verses.translation: But when Rama said thus, Khara is infuriated and convulsed in anger, and he replied Rama with bloodshot eyes, laughing boisterously.
notes: dhvani/allusion: Khara 'laughed at' Rama's words of self-praise means that even the Supreme Being untiringly does some self-praise like telling 'I am here to save you... seek refuge in me for I alone can save...' in order to make Himself known to the adamants. The whole concept of Bhagavad Gita in telling that 'I am here... Know me thus...' etc., is for the same purpose. Thus, this is a laughable situation to those who are already in the know of Being. Presently it is Khara who was great Vedic Brahman once, but became an ogre by curse. Contrariwise, it is a 'laughable talk' of the Supreme Being, to non-knowers or for the non-adherers.

glosses.meaning: by Rama, thus, [Khara is] said, but

verses.devanagari:
प्राकृतान् राक्षसान् हत्वा युद्धे दशरथ आत्मज |
आत्मना कथम् आत्मानम् अप्रशस्यम् प्रशंससि
verses.iast:
prākṛtān rākṣasān hatvā yuddhe daśaratha ātmaja |
ātmanā katham ātmānam apraśasyam praśaṃsasi
verses.translation: "On killing average demons in war, oh, son of Dasharatha, how you praise yourself when you yourself are un-praiseworthy?" Thus Khara started to speak to Rama.
notes: dhvani/allusion: For this self-praise it is said that Khara estimated Rama as an unworthy being in the parlance of mortals. kharaḥ tu kopāt asamartho rāma iti bhrāntā uktavān iti no ko api doṣaḥ | dk But as a cursed Vedic Brahman who is in the know of Rama as Vishnu is retorting Rama saying 'you also need to self-eulogise, when I am fully aware of you and come hither to gain my salvation at your hand? You are not supposed to self-extol before small beings like us...'

glosses.meaning: in war, primitive - average, demons, on killing

verses.devanagari:
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तो वा ये भवन्ति नरर्षभाः |
कथयन्ति न ते किंचित् तेजसा स्वेन गर्विताः
verses.iast:
vikrāntā balavanto vā ye bhavanti nararṣabhāḥ |
kathayanti na te kiñcit tejasā svena garvitāḥ
verses.translation: "Those best of men that are victorious and mighty will not boast anything, for they will be really proud of their own valour.
notes: dhvani/allusion: This is said otherwise: ye nararṣabhāḥ 'those best ones among men like you...' te 'by them...' [adhyāhārya] evam 'elliptic: this way...' na kathayanti 'do not praise themselves...' tejasā svena garvitāḥ kathayanti some of 'those that are proud of their own valorous resplendence, they speak up their glory, vaingloriously...' 'So it is unapt of you to speak up for yourself, for we are in the know of it, and we are waiting for our release from our curse at your hand...' Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: they, of their own, with valour, becoming proud

verses.devanagari:
प्राकृताः तु अकृत आत्मानो लोके क्षत्रिय पांसनाः |
निरर्थकम् विकत्थन्ते यथा राम विकत्थसे
verses.iast:
prākṛtāḥ tu akṛta ātmāno loke kṣatriya pāṃsanāḥ |
nirarthakam vikatthante yathā rāma vikatthase
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, as to how undignified Kshatriya-s that are frivolous and irresolute in self-confidence will boast in the world, likewise you too are boasting in a meaningless manner.
notes: dhvani/allusion: Khara's intent is: kṣatriya pāmsanāḥ 'the Kshatriya, worthless... worthless Kshatriya-s...' yathā nir arthakam vikatthase 'as to how they meaninglessly speak up for themselves...' rāma tvam vikatthante 'oh, Rama, you are speaking like that...' 'It is unapt of you to talk vainly like any other average Kshatriya, as you are an incarnate in a best Kshatriya clan, and you do your duty righteously without much talk...' Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: not, perfected, with selves - irresolute in self-confidence
as to how, they are boasting
not, meaningful, verily, they speak up - you boast in a meaningless manner.

verses.devanagari:
कुलम् व्यपदिशन् वीरः समरे को अभिधास्यति |
मृत्यु काले हि संप्राप्ते स्वयम् अप्रस्तवे स्तवम्
verses.iast:
kulam vyapadiśan vīraḥ samare ko abhidhāsyati |
mṛtyu kāle hi samprāpte svayam aprastave stavam
verses.translation: "Who will be that valiant that speaks about his lineage at wartime, that too, when the death-time is looming large! And, there will there be someone who broaches his self-extols in such an inopportune situation, is it!
notes: dhvani/allusion: Khara's saying is: samare 'in war...' [adhyāhāra]: śatru pakśe 'elliptic: on the enemy's side...' mṛtyu kāle samprāpte sati 'death time, while chancing, that being so...' stavam ko vā abhidāsyati 'self-praise, who, either, speaks out...' Thus, Khara's saying is: 'where is the necessity for any warrior to self-eulogise when the death-time is hovering upon his enemy? And you, as Rama, are on the winning spree in this war, and there is no necessity to extol yourself...' Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: at death, time, on arrival of - looming large
who, in wartime, his lineage, while speaking about

verses.devanagari:
सर्वथा तु लघुत्वम् ते कत्थनेन विदर्शितम् |
सुवर्ण प्रतिरूपेण तप्तेन इव कुश अग्निना
verses.iast:
sarvathā tu laghutvam te katthanena vidarśitam |
suvarṇa pratirūpeṇa taptena iva kuśa agninā
verses.translation: "Howsoever your ignominy is well shown by your self-praise, like the manifestation of gold on the tip of grass-blade burnt by fire, where the fire on grass-blade is no fire, and the bulb of fire appearing at the tip of grass-blade as a bulb of gold, is no gold.
notes: dhvani/allusion: A blade of grass when burnt, immediately glows and manifests a globe of golden flame, but it is too quick to evanish thus it can not burn the gold to refine it. katthanena 'by broaching...' te laghutvam 'your ignominy...' sarvathaiva vidarśitam ' in every way, well-shown...' and that ignominy is looking like taptena 'burnt...' kuśa agninā 'fire abiding the grass-blade...' suvarṇa pratirūpeṇa 'golden in hue...' laghutvam vidarśyate yathā tathā 'lowliness of fire proper will be shown by that fire on grass-blade, likewise... tava laghutvam eva vidarśitam bhavat 'so also your own lowliness is made evident...' 'A small fire on a small grass-blade quickly burns though with a golden hue, but it cannot sustain its flame to burn other things. It burns the grass-blade on which it sits. So, self-ruinous is your self-eulogy...' Govindaraja.

kuśa agninā 'by grass-blade's fire...' that is used to purify golden material in rituals; suvarṇa prati rūpeṇa 'gold, equalling in aspect...' namely brass items; taptena 'if burnt to purify...'; laghutvam 'stain of blakishness...'; If brass items are put to the same small fire of grass-blade they immediately become smoky, however small the fire may be; Thus te 'by you...' katthanena 'by self-praising...' laghutvam vidarśitam 'your futility is well-shown...' Maheshvara Tiirtha.

suvarṇa prati rūpeṇa tapyatena aśmanā agninā is another text. In this aśmanā is 'stone...' If anyone touches a stone that is similar to fire outwardly, he does not feel the heat of the fire by the cold touch of stone. Thus, his 'foolishly mistaken identity' makes a fool of himself. Thus Khara is saying 'I was thinking that Rama is a very great valiant person, but by way of listening your self-eulogies, at an inopportune time, you appear to be a cold stone but not a firebrand... One who goes on self-eulogising without taking any action in a war is a coward but not a victor...' Thus Khara is quickening Rama to proceed with fighting so that the ensuing salvation can also be quickened.

glosses.meaning: golden, in reflection, aspect - having the aspect of gold

verses.devanagari:
न तु माम् इह तिष्ठंतम् पश्यसि त्वम् गदा धरम् |
धराधरम् इव अकंप्यम् पर्वतम् धातुभिः चितम्
verses.iast:
na tu mām iha tiṣṭhaṃtam paśyasi tvam gadā dharam |
dharādharam iva akampyam parvatam dhātubhiḥ citam
verses.translation: "But you are seeing me wielding a mace and standing before you like an unshakable and jagged mountain laden with ores, isn't it!

glosses.meaning: me, but, not, you see, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
पर्याप्तो अहम् गदा पाणिर् हन्तुम् प्राणान् रणे तव |
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानाम् पाश हस्त इव अंतकः
verses.iast:
paryāpto aham gadā pāṇir hantum prāṇān raṇe tava |
trayāṇām api lokānām pāśa hasta iva aṃtakaḥ
verses.translation: "As to how the Terminator wielding noose is enough to take away all the lives in all the three worlds, handling my mace I am enough for detracting your life from you.
notes: dhvani/allusion: 'I am not competent enough to combat with you...' is the sense that is drawn out. gadā dharam mām paśyasi nanu 'mace-wielder, me, you see, though...' 'Though you see me wielding this mace...' pāśa hasta antaka iva 'noose-wielder Yama, Terminator, like...' 'Though I appear to be noose-wielding Terminator...' trayaṇām api lokānām prāṇān hantum paryāptaḥ yadyapi tathā api 'Though I can strike down the lives of all in all the three worlds with this single mace as Yama does so with only one noose...' raṇe tava na paryāptaḥ 'in war, with you, not, competent... 'I am not competent enough to fight with you in war, for I am an inferior being in comparison to you, oh, Supreme Being...'

glosses.meaning: for three, worlds, even for the [lives in those three worlds,] as with
in war, your, lives, to destroy - to kill
with mace, in hand, I am, enough.

verses.devanagari:
कामम् बहु अपि वक्तव्यम् त्वयि वक्ष्यामि न तु अहम् |
अस्तम् प्राप्नोति सविता युद्ध विघ्नः ततो भवेत्
verses.iast:
kāmam bahu api vaktavyam tvayi vakṣyāmi na tu aham |
astam prāpnoti savitā yuddha vighnaḥ tato bhavet
verses.translation: "Even though much is to be said in your respect I will not continue to say, for the sun is getting at the dusk thereby disruption to war occurs.
notes: dhvani/allusion: This is the devil's advocacy about dharma yuddha 'righteous warfare...' which righteous war is generally waged from morning till evening. Khara says that 'because the sun is dusking you humans cannot war with us, the nightwalkers who are adept in night-wars. Thus by killing you in nighttime does not prove my victory, for your warfare is from sunrise to sunset. Hence, this war is to be stalled. If you quicken now without self-extolling, I will kill you before sunset, proving my chivalry and then I can dab the eyes of the wives of the demons so far killed by you...'

glosses.meaning: much, is to be said, though, really
I am, not, tell - I will not continue to say

verses.devanagari:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि राक्षसानाम् हतानि ते |
त्वत् विनाशात् करोमि अद्य तेषाम् अश्रु प्रमार्जनम्
verses.iast:
caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rākṣasānām hatāni te |
tvat vināśāt karomi adya teṣām aśru pramārjanam
verses.translation: "You have killed fourteen thousand demons and on killing you I will wipe the tears of the wives of those dead demons today itself." Khara said so to Rama.
notes: dhvani/allusion: Khara cannot return to his place after sacrificing these many demons. Either he should win or be won over. So 'when these many demons are eliminated by you... tvad vināśāt = tvattaḥ nāśāt 'by you if I am eliminated...' eṣām aśru pramārjanam karomi 'their tears I will wipe... 'For I sacrificed fourteen thousand kinsmen of mine, and if I am also killed by you, their wives do not find fault with me and my death will wipe their tears out... that is why, though you tried to pacify and avert me from warring with soft talk mṛdu pūrva bhāṣaṇena, as at 3-29-1. I can not but war, and you need not think that I am heedless of your words...' Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: on your, utter, eradication - on killing you

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा परम क्रुद्धः ताम् गदाम् परम अन्गदाम् |
खरः चिक्षेप रामाय प्रदीप्ताम् अशनिम् यथा
verses.iast:
iti uktvā parama kruddhaḥ tām gadām parama angadām |
kharaḥ cikṣepa rāmāya pradīptām aśanim yathā
verses.translation: Saying thus that highly infuriated Khara hurled his mace towards Rama, around which there are superb golden cinctures, and which is extremely glaring like a thunderbolt.

glosses.meaning: one who has superb bicep-lets, Khara]
extremely glaring, thunderbolt, which is like

verses.devanagari:
खर बाहु प्रमुक्ता सा प्रदीप्ता महती गदा |
भस्म वृक्षाम् च गुल्माम् च कृत्वा अगात् तत् समीपतः
verses.iast:
khara bāhu pramuktā sā pradīptā mahatī gadā |
bhasma vṛkṣām ca gulmām ca kṛtvā agāt tat samīpataḥ
verses.translation: Forcefully discharged from Khara's hands that highly fiery and stupendous mace rendering trees and shrubs down to ashes darted towards Rama.

glosses.meaning: to ashes, making - on rendering down
to his [Rama's,] near, has gone - darted out.

verses.devanagari:
ताम् आपतन्तीम् महतीम् मृत्यु पाश उपमाम् गदाम् |
अंतरिक्ष गताम् रामः चिच्छ्हेद बहुधा शरैः
verses.iast:
tām āpatantīm mahatīm mṛtyu pāśa upamām gadām |
aṃtarikṣa gatām rāmaḥ cicchheda bahudhā śaraiḥ
verses.translation: When that monstrous mace similar to the halter of the Terminator is swooping down, Rama smashed it to smithereens with his arrows while it is still sky rocketing.

glosses.meaning: Rama, with arrows, variously, smashed - to smithereens.

verses.devanagari:
सा विशीर्णा शरैः भिन्ना पपात धरणी तले |
गदा मंत्र औषधि बलैर् व्याली इव विनिपातिता
verses.iast:
sā viśīrṇā śaraiḥ bhinnā papāta dharaṇī tale |
gadā maṃtra auṣadhi balair vyālī iva vinipātitā
verses.translation: That mace splintered with arrows of Rama fell crumbling onto the surface of earth as a springing female snake would fall down by the strength of spells and nostrums.
notes: dhvani/allusion: The mention about Khara's mace may be noticed. In the text, its reference has come more often and at the end it is said to have burnt down the vegetation along its course of travel, which indicates that it has some radiation power. Without making it to touch the ground, Rama has splintered it in sky itself, and its destruction is metaphoric with a venomous serpent, and hymns and herbs can bring down that serpent. That is to say even if venomous missiles are used their antidotes are ready at hand. For this Dharmaakuutam says, without expanding: anena mantra auṣadhi balaiḥ viṣa ādi nāśa ukto bhavati | dk 'any poison can be neutralised by antidotes, say spells and nostrums...'

glosses.meaning: by spells, by nostrums, by the strengths of
utterly, down, fallen came to naught
